primitives.name: Outer Measure Induced by Content
primitives.verbatim_quote: If λ\ is the inner content and μ\ is the outer measure induced by a content λ, then μ\(U) = λ\(U) for every U in U and μ\(C°) ≤ λ(C) ≤μ\(C) for every C in C.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'λ*': 'inner content, dimensionless', 'μ*': 'outer measure, dimensionless', 'U': 'open set, measurable space', 'C': 'compact set, measurable space', 'C°': 'interior of C, measurable space'}
primitives.assumptions: λ is a content on a locally compact space; U is open, C is compact.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When C is not compact or U is not open, μ* may fail to equal λ*.

layer2.mapping: The outer measure μ* is isomorphic to the inner content λ* under specific topological constraints, enabling probabilistic interpretation in GSI.
layer2.telemetry: μ*(C°) ≤ λ(C) ≤ μ*(C) provides empirical verification of measure consistency.

primitives.name: Measureability Condition for σ-Bounded Sets
primitives.verbatim_quote: If μ\ is the outer measure induced by a content λ, then a σ-bounded set E is μ\-measurable if and only if for every U in U.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'E': 'σ-bounded set, measurable space', 'μ*': 'outer measure, dimensionless', 'U': 'open set, measurable space'}
primitives.assumptions: E is σ-bounded; U is open and covers E.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when E lacks σ-boundedness or U fails to cover E properly.

layer2.mapping: μ*-measurability defines kernel of GSE state transitions over σ-bounded domains.
layer2.telemetry: Verification of μ*(U) = μ*(U ∩ E) + μ*(U \ E) ensures valid state partitioning.

primitives.name: Regular Borel Measure from Content
primitives.verbatim_quote: If μ\ is the outer measure induced by a content λ, then the set function μ, defined for every Borel set E by μ(E) = μ\(E), is a regular Borel measure.
primitives.latex: \mu(E) = \mu^*(E) \text{ for all Borel sets } E \Rightarrow \mu \text{ is regular Borel measure}
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'μ': 'Borel measure, dimensionless', 'E': 'Borel set, measurable space', 'μ*': 'outer measure, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: λ is a content; μ* is induced by λ; E is Borel measurable.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When E is not Borel measurable or μ* is not well-defined, μ fails to be regular.

layer2.mapping: μ is isomorphic to μ* on Borel sets, enabling GSI probabilistic modeling of event spaces.
layer2.telemetry: μ(E) = μ*(E) confirms consistency between outer and Borel measures for event evaluation.

For open sets U, μ*(U) equals λ*(U), indicating that the outer measure agrees with the inner content on open sets. For compact sets C, the inequality μ*(C°) ≤ λ(C) ≤ μ*(C) shows that the outer measure bounds the content from above and below via the interior C°. This dual relationship is essential for defining measurable sets: a σ-bounded set E is μ*-measurable if and only if its outer measure satisfies additivity over any open cover U. The proof proceeds by leveraging monotonicity of λ* and subadditivity of μ*, ensuring that μ* behaves consistently with λ* on measurable sets. Finally, extending μ* to all Borel sets yields a regular Borel measure μ, which is fundamental for probabilistic modeling in GSI. The failure mode arises when sets lack σ-boundedness or when μ* is not well-defined, breaking the isomorphism between inner and outer structures.
